title: Carvera post: support the 4th-axis rotary module (A axis) and the built-in laser module

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

The Carvera post writes 3-axis milling programs only.

1. The post refuses each tilted or rotary record. The message is "the 4th axis module is not supported yet". A user cannot post a job for the Carvera 4th-axis rotary module.
2. The post declares milling only. It writes no laser-mode start or end. A user cannot post a job for the Carvera laser module.

These refusals are safe. The post makes no wrong output.

## Expected

1. A 4th-axis job on a Carvera posts with an `A` word. The Carvera manual states that the A axis has no separate work and machine coordinates. The post must obey that rule.
2. A laser job on a Carvera posts with the laser mode of the Carvera manual:
   - `M321` starts laser mode. The control drops the spindle tool and calibrates the laser.
   - `G0Z0` moves to the laser focus height.
   - `M322` stops laser mode at the end.

## Evidence

Main `8937e684d`:

- `assets/posts/carvera.cps:14`: the description says "3-axis mill".
- `assets/posts/carvera.cps:21`: `capabilities = 1` (milling only).
- `assets/posts/carvera.cps:175-177`: `tiltOk()` refuses tilted records. The calls are at `:492`, `:498` and `:509`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/carvera/rotary.refusal`: this golden pins the refusal.
- The post has no `M321` or `M322`.
- Makera Carvera instruction manual v1.0: the 4th-axis module on printed pages 26-27, 49-51 and 55; the laser mode codes on printed pages 28-29, 53 and 55.

Related: #4081 (laser profile operation). Its scope item 4 asks for a post dialect for a laser control. The Carvera laser mode can be that dialect.

Found by the post audit against the Makera manuals (#4130).

## Done means

- A Carvera machine file can declare the A-axis module. The post then writes `A` words for a 4th-axis (indexed or rotary) job. When the module is not declared, the refusal stays.
- A laser operation on a Carvera posts `M321`, `G0Z0`, the cut and `M322`. A golden pins this output.
- The `rotary.refusal` golden stays for a machine without the module.
